title: How and when sell approvals are sent, and which fee ceiling applies to them and to the public fallback

options.name: Keep current behaviour: exact-amount public approve right before each sell, ethers default fees, no ceiling
options.risk: Every first exit waits for a public approve (an unbounded wait, AUD-EXIT-009), signals the sell, and pays fees outside the ceiling (AUD-EXIT-004).

options.name: Approve the router once right after the buy lands (bounded or max allowance to that one router)
options.behavior_impact: Exits, including anti-rug, start with the private sell at once.
options.risk: A standing allowance to the router; an extra tx per buy.

options.name: Put the approve in the same private bundle as the sell
options.behavior_impact: No public approve; one private inclusion.
options.risk: Only where the strategy supports multi-tx bundles (not passthrough chains).

options.name: Keep approving at exit time but apply the sell fee ceiling and anti-rug fee policy to approvals and the public fallback
options.risk: Keeps the latency and the public signal.

recommendation: approve-at-buy plus the ceiling for whatever approves remain.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). Capital-relevant, but the linked findings are S2 or lower, so the default is safe to rest on until then.
behavior_impact: Decides how much delay and public signal stand in front of every exit.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
